Notre travail ne se limite pas à offrir à nos clients un enregistrement et un départ sans problème. Nous devons avant tout bâtir une expérience unique et mémorable. Nos experts en Expérience client prennent l'initiative d'offrir un vaste éventail de services qui guident les clients tout au long de leur séjour. Ils sont habilités à se déplacer dans leur espace et à faire ce qui doit être fait. Que ce soit traiter les besoins opérationnels, répondre aux demandes des clients, préparer des rapports ou partager les points d'intérêt de la région, les experts en Expérience client font en sorte que les clients sentent que les transactions font partie de l'expérience.

Peu importe votre poste, certaines choses sont essentielles pour réussir - la création d'un lieu de travail sécuritaire, le respect des politiques et des procédures de la société, le maintien de la confidentialité, la protection des actifs de la société, le respect des normes de qualité et veiller à ce que votre uniforme, votre apparence personnelle et vos communications soient professionnels. Le rôle d'expert en Expérience client signifie être sur vos pieds et vous déplacer (se lever, s’asseoir ou marcher pendant une longue période de temps) et mettre la main à la pâte dans votre travail (déplacer, soulever, porter, pousser, tirer et placer des objets pesant jusqu’à 10 livres (4,5 kg) sans assistance). Il est essentiel que les experts en Expérience client exécutent toutes ces tâches à la perfection (et toute autre tâche raisonnable qui leur est assignée) - ainsi, nos clients seront toujours satisfaits et notre entreprise continuera de prospérer.

d: Tamara is the leading fintech platform in Saudi Arabia and the wider GCC region with a mission to help people make their dreams come true by building the most customer-centric financial super-app on earth. The company serves millions of users in KSA, UAE and Kuwait, and partners with leading global and regional brands such as SHEIN, Jarir, noon, Amazon, IKEA, eXtra and Farfetch as well as small and medium businesses.

r: The Head of Procurement & Vendor Management will build and lead Tamara’s procurement function from the ground up, owning the full vendor lifecycle across the Tamara group: from planning demand and choosing vendors, through negotiation, signing and onboarding, to performance management, renewal and exit.

This is a first-of-its-kind role at Tamara. You will turn a decentralised contracting landscape into one governed, auditable process; take custody of our new contract lifecycle management (CLM) platform; and make sure every vendor and outsourcing arrangement meets SAMA, CBUAE and listed-company standards, without slowing the business down.

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, with a dotted line to the General Counsel on contract governance, you will lead a team of two Procurement & Vendor Associates to start. You will be the single point of coordination between the business, Legal, Finance, GRC, Information Security, Compliance and People on every vendor decision.
Define and deliver Tamara’s group-wide procurement and vendor management strategy, aligned with business plans.

Write and maintain the Procurement Policy, Vendor Management Standard and supporting procedures, and, with GRC and Legal, the Outsourcing Policy that SAMA requires the Board to approve and review every year.
Set the sourcing rules: spend thresholds, the minimum number of quotations, when a competitive tender is required, and when single or sole sourcing is allowed and how it is justified and approved.
Co-design and enforce the procurement elements of the Delegation of Authority (DoA) with Finance and Legal: who may request, approve, commit and sign, and up to what value.
Build segregation of duties into the procure-to-pay cycle, so that no one person can request, select, approve, receive and pay for the same purchase.
Make “no contract, no purchase order; no purchase order, no payment” standard practice, with a clear and limited exceptions process.
Run an annual and quarterly demand-planning cycle with budget owners and FP&A, so that major purchases and renewals are known before they become urgent.
Own a single front door for all purchase requests, triaged by value, risk and category, with turnaround times the business can rely on.
Check every commitment against approved budget before it is signed, not after.
Lead RFIs, RFPs and RFQs, with documented evaluation criteria, scoring and decision records.
Lead or support major commercial negotiations on price, payment terms, service levels, liability, termination and exit, in partnership with Legal on contractual terms and frameworks.
Build category strategies for Tamara’s main spend areas, including technology and cloud, outsourced operations, marketing, professional services, people services and facilities.
Consolidate the vendor base, remove duplicate tools and contracts, and report verified savings and cost avoidance to Finance.

Run a risk-based onboarding process for every new vendor, with Compliance: company registration and ownership (KYB), sanctions and adverse-media screening, financial health, and conflicts of interest.

Coordinate information security and data protection assessments with Information Security and the Data Protection Officer, covering SAMA Cyber Security Framework third-party controls and Saudi Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) requirements.
With GRC, classify each arrangement by criticality and as material or non-material outsourcing, and prepare SAMA (and, where applicable, CBUAE) non-objection requests on time.
Identify related-party transactions and conflicts of interest early, so they follow the approval and disclosure path expected of a listed company.
Protect the vendor master from fraud with Payables: controlled vendor creation, independently verified bank-detail changes, and removal of inactive vendors.

Ensure every vendor agreement uses a Legal-approved template or is reviewed by Legal, and contains the required clauses: SLAs, audit and regulator access rights, data protection, information security, sub-contracting consent, business continuity, incident notification and exit support.

Run the approval and signing workflow end to end: the right approvers under the DoA, authorised signatories only, e-signature where possible, and a fully executed copy stored before any work or payment starts.

Take custody of the CLM platform: migrate group-wide vendor agreements, keep contract records complete (owner, value, term, renewal and notice dates, criticality), and drive adoption across the business.
Issue and manage purchase orders, and hand over cleanly to Payables for goods and services receipt, three-way matching and payment.
Agree with Finance the controls, accrual inputs and month-end information that procurement provides.
Assign a business owner to every contract and set up tiered reviews: quarterly business reviews for critical vendors and scorecards for the rest.
Track SLAs, breaches, service credits and incidents with business owners; escalate and remediate, and alert GRC to any event that may need reporting to regulators.

Monitor critical and outsourced vendors on an ongoing basis, including financial health, security posture, concentration risk and their own sub-contractors, and keep exit and continuity plans up to date.
Maintain a group renewal calendar with enough lead time to renegotiate, re-tender or exit, including the 30-working-day SAMA non-objection lead time for renewing material outsourcing.
Manage amendments, change orders and terminations, with Legal leading on disputes.
Run orderly exits: transition to a new vendor, return or deletion of Tamara data, removal of system and premises access, and final settlement.
Legal: templates, legal review, negotiation of legal terms and disputes. Procurement owns the commercial process and manages the contract after signing.
Finance: budget approval, FP&A, Payables and accruals. Procurement owns the commitment before it reaches Finance.
GRC & Risk: third-party risk standards, outsourcing materiality and regulatory reporting. Procurement runs the first-line controls.
Information Security & Data Protection: vendor security and privacy assessments, and data processing terms.
Compliance: KYB, sanctions, anti-bribery, gifts and hospitality, and conflicts of interest.
People: recruitment agencies, contingent workforce, benefits, training and other people vendors, employee conflict-of-interest declarations and the procurement code of conduct.
Internal Audit and external auditors: evidence that controls work, and audit readiness.
Budget owners in Technology, Product, Marketing, Operations and Commercial: day-to-day vendor relationships, supported by procurement.

Maintain the group outsourcing register and report to the Executive Committee, the relevant Board committees and regulators as required: spend under management, savings, vendor risk, contract coverage, SLA performance and policy exceptions.
Own procurement systems and data, including the CLM platform and sourcing and spend tools, and automate approvals and reporting.
Hire, lead and develop the procurement team, starting with two associates, and build the case for scaling it as Tamara grows.
Train budget owners and requesters across the group on how to buy at Tamara.
A complete map of active vendors and contracts across group entities, with owners and renewal dates.
An outsourcing register with every arrangement classified by materiality, and a plan for any outstanding SAMA or CBUAE notifications.
Interim controls live for intake, budget check and signing while the full policy is approved.
A phased plan, agreed with Legal, to migrate group vendor agreements into the CLM platform.
Draft Procurement and Outsourcing policies ready for Executive and Board review.
Procurement and Outsourcing policies approved by the Board and adopted across the group.
All active vendor agreements in the CLM platform, with complete records and named owners.

d: Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.
The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.
We build internal systems to the same standard as our public products: specified, tested, reviewed and observable. We want engineers who enjoy that rigour and take full ownership of what they ship.
q: Treat testing, security, performance and accessibility as part of the job
Handle sensitive people data with care
Write clearly and work well in a distributed team
Own your work from first spec to production
Nice to have: Python, Go, React, Svelte, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes, a history of building tools for HR, finance or operations.

The ideal candidate will use their passion for experimentation and analytics to build tomorrow’s tech organisation. This team will help us gain insights into the business and our talent pool, and use those insights to improve the experience of working at Canonical.

As a Workplace Engineer at Canonical, you need an analytical, data-driven mind and a passion to connect and make sense of interesting data from APIs. We focus heavily on the collection of metrics, optimising processes, and ways of working across Canonical. You need to demonstrate leadership, excellence, and consistency and will mentor others in the team.

Build Go services and APIs that connect many data sources
Design data models and architecture for connected systems
Turn data into clear dashboards and visualisations
Build LLM-powered features into everyday workflows
Write specs, estimate work and deliver to agreed criteria
Set a high bar in code review, testing and documentation
Partner with non-technical colleagues to turn needs into tools
Mentor engineers and improve how the team works
